en: Hahahaha...
I'm Vanessa.
I run an inn.
I do hope we meet again.
Would you care to join me for tea?
How about tonight, perhaps?
At my inn, I'd offer you special services.
note: Innuendo kept (she runs the inn as a brothel).

en: I run the inn here,
and my name is Vanessa.
I'm off to mind the front desk at the inn.
Say, do come by my inn tonight,
won't you? Hm?
For a charming young man like you, I'd
offer all sorts of special services.
Hmm, maybe I'll stop by one of these days.
Just head north from this café
and you'll find it.
It's simple.
They stay the night with a gentleman, and
get a meal and a bed at my inn. That's all.
Welcome to the inn...
Please, tell me whatever you wish.
Am I working too hard? I feel dizzy.
But I'm hurt, and yet it doesn't hurt at all.
I'll do just as you command.
The woman next door and I both had bruises
on our faces. As if we'd been in a fistfight.
Um, excuse me...
Good morning, young lady.
Is there something you want of me?
Oh, um, you look like a fine gentleman, so
there's something I really must ask you.
...Would you have any work that I
could do?
Childcare, cleaning, laundry: I'll do anything.
Well, well, looking for work? How awkward.
I manage perfectly well on my own.
Why not try elsewhere?
I-I see...
Sorry for the bother. Please excuse me.
Um, my name is Beth.
If there's anything I can do, please tell
me... I'm begging you!
...I still haven't found any work...
At this rate, I can't make a decent living.
Good morning. Lovely morning, isn't it?
I've found a job!
Mind you, it's only for a month.
I'll do my best to make a life in London.
Good evening, um...
Good evening, young lady. What's the matter?
I'm sorry, um...
Would you have need of a maid or a nanny?
My name is Beth.
Could you take me on in your household?
Well, well, this is rather sudden.
I live alone, so I've no need of a nanny.
I can manage most things myself. Sorry.
I-I see...
I'm sorry for stopping you like that.
Excuse me...
I'm sorry about earlier...
Are you on your way home from work?
This may sound
rude of me, but
men are lucky to have so many kinds of work.
Even in London, the jobs a woman can earn
money at are few and far between. It's hard.
Oh, did I tell you that already?
It's cleaning a diner, but I'll do my best.
Sorry for all the trouble I caused you.
Good day, young lady. Pardon me.
I'll just take a book from the top shelf.
Oh! Ah, um, go right ahead.
What is the matter? You look downcast.
Though perhaps it's none of my business.
Not at all...
I came to London to find work, and this
bookshop kindly took me on, but...
